title: Third pillar of Islam – fasting
intro: Fasting in the month of Ramadan is the third duty of Islam.

learn.html: The third pillar of Islam – the third main Islamic duty – is fasting in the month of Ramadan.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah tells the believers that fasting has been prescribed for them as it was prescribed for those before them, so that they may become mindful of Allah (taqwa). (Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:183)
Fasting means knowingly holding back from food, drink and other bodily pleasures from the start of dawn until sunset. The Ramadan fast means:

items: starting the fast on time, with the niyyah
during the day, staying away from everything that breaks the fast

learn.label: The niyyah for the fast
learn.ar: نَوَيْتُ أَنْ أَصُومَ غَدًا فَرِيضَةً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى
learn.tr: Nawaytu an asooma ghadan fareedatan min shahri Ramadaana lillaahi ta‘aalaa.
learn.en: I intend to fast tomorrow the obligatory fast of the month of Ramadan, for Allah, the Most High.

learn.label: The dua for iftar
learn.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي لَكَ صُمْتُ وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ وَعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَى رِزْقِكَ أَفْطَرْتُ
learn.tr: Allaahumma innee laka sumtu, wa bika aamantu, wa ‘alayka tawakkaltu, wa ‘alaa rizqika aftartu.
learn.en: O Allah, for You I fasted, in You I believe, in You I trust, and with Your provision I break my fast.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “When one of you breaks the fast, let him break it with a date; if he cannot find a date, then with water, for water is pure.” (Tirmidhi)

learn.text: In Ramadan it is lovely to…

items: pray all the prayers in jama‘ah if we can
read the Qur’an or its translation
hold iftars with family, neighbours and friends
spend lots of time in dhikr, dua and salawat on the Prophet (SAW)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: At the end of Ramadan every person who fasts must give sadaqat al-fitr, which cleans the fast from bad and useless talk.

items.label: Muqabalah – reading the Qur’an together in the masjid
Tarawih – a special prayer on Ramadan nights after Isha
I‘tikaf – staying in the masjid in the last ten days only for worship
Suhur – the meal before the fast, until dawn
Imsak – the moment the fast begins
Iftar – the time the fast ends
